explanation: The padded input has H + 2p pixels. The first window uses eff_k of them; every further window needs `stride` more, so floor((H + 2p - eff_k)/stride) extra windows fit, plus the first one.

title: SmallCNN forward pass
description: Forward pass of a two-conv CNN that returns raw class scores (logits) for a batch: conv/ReLU/pool twice, flatten each image, then two linear layers.
code:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def forward(self, x):
    x = F.max_pool2d(F.relu(self.conv1(x)), kernel_size=2, stride=2)
    x = F.max_pool2d(F.relu(self.conv2(x)), kernel_size=2, stride=2)
    x = torch.flatten(x, start_dim=0)
    x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))
    x = F.softmax(self.fc2(x), dim=1)
    return x

errors.explanation: start_dim=0 flattens the batch axis too, merging all images into one vector. Keep dim 0.
The model must return raw logits: cross_entropy applies log-softmax itself, so an extra softmax distorts the loss.

hints: One bug concerns shape, one concerns the output activation.

title: One training epoch
description: Trains a classifier for one pass over a loader and returns the sample-weighted average loss and the accuracy of the predictions made before each update.
code:
def train_one_epoch(model, loader, optimizer, device):
    model.eval()
    total_loss, total_correct, total_samples = 0.0, 0, 0
    for images, labels in loader:
        batch_size = images.shape[0]
        images, labels = images.to(device), labels
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        logits = model(images)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        total_loss += loss.item()
        total_correct += (logits.argmax(dim=1) == labels).sum().item()
        total_samples += batch_size
    return {"loss": total_loss / total_samples, "accuracy": total_correct / total_samples}

errors.explanation: Training must run in train mode (dropout/batch-norm active); eval() is for evaluation.
The labels also have to be moved to the model's device, otherwise the loss mixes CPU and GPU tensors.
loss.item() is a per-batch mean; weight it by the batch size so a smaller final batch counts proportionally.

hints: Think about mode, device placement and averaging.
Which tensors are moved to the device? How is the epoch loss accumulated?
model.train(); labels.to(device); loss.item() * batch_size.
